name: Should I keep my bathroom vanity in the same place or move it?

mainEntity.name: Should I keep my bathroom vanity in the same place or move it?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Keep the new vanity in the same location when the goal is a lower-cost, lower-disruption update. Change the layout only when the current position causes storage, clearance, accessibility, or plumbing problems that justify added design and construction work.

Context: Moving a vanity can affect drains, supply lines, outlets, lighting, flooring, mirrors, and wall finishes. Elite Remodeling & Design can evaluate layout options through design development and 3D visualization when the replacement is part of a larger bathroom transformation.

Key factors:
- Door and shower clearance
- Existing plumbing access
- Natural and artificial lighting
- Storage and daily-use patterns

Practical guidance: Draw the room to scale and mark doors, fixtures, and cabinet swing before approving a new location. Include service access and future maintenance in the plan.

A modest layout improvement can add value, but only when its benefits outweigh added scope.
acceptedAnswer.description: Keep the location for the simplest and usually least disruptive replacement. Move it only when the current layout creates real clearance, storage, accessibility, or functionality problems, because relocation can affect plumbing, electrical work, flooring, mirrors, and permits.
